## Summary

Implemented SPEC.md §4 (Health/HealthKit), scoped to Health.vue only:

- **`App_Resources/iOS/app.entitlements`** (new) — HealthKit entitlement.
- **`App_Resources/iOS/Info.plist`** — added `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` / `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription`.
- **`app/components/Health.vue`** — wired to `HKHealthStore`: authorization status/request (§4.1), 500-step logging via `HKQuantitySample` (§4.2), and a 7-day daily-sum query via `HKSampleQuery` with exact label formatting and thousands separators, denied/no-data states (§4.3). Status line refreshes on every `navigatedTo`. All native errors are caught and surfaced in the status line, never console-only.
- **`types/references.d.ts`** — added a reference to the HealthKit typings, which the project's default type-reference chain excludes (it only pulls in a "common" framework subset). This fixed 27 `vue-tsc` errors; the Xcode build itself was unaffected either way since the Babel-based bundler doesn't type-check.

Verified: `ns build ios` succeeds with zero errors, and I installed/launched the built app on a booted Simulator — it launches and stays alive without crashing, with the Home screen rendering correctly. I wasn't able to interactively tap through the Health screen's permission/logging flow — this sandbox lacks the Accessibility permission `osascript`/System Events needs to drive UI taps — so that live flow (permission prompt, granted/denied states, step logging, 7-day list) is verified by code review against the actual installed HealthKit type declarations rather than by interactive testing.
